rules.legal_concept: Right of any person to inspect public records
rules.atomic_rule: All public records shall be open for inspection by any person, except as otherwise provided by the act; each public agency must make suitable facilities available for inspection.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of access)
rules.source_language: All public records shall be open for inspection by any person, except as otherwise provided by this act, and suitable facilities shall be made available by each public agency for this purpose.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared eligibility key. 'Any person' carries no requester-class limitation.

rules.atomic_rule: No residency or citizenship qualification is imposed on the right to request; the right runs to 'any person.'
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: All public records shall be open for inspection by any person, except as otherwise provided by this act, and suitable facilities shall be made available by each public agency for this purpose.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule (not a negative). Kansas grants access to 'any person'; no residency qualifier appears in the act. Same operative clause as KS-0001.

rules.legal_concept: No general statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency shall not require a request to contain more than the requester's name and address and the information necessary to ascertain the records and the requester's right of access; no general statement of purpose is required.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by subsection (c), a public agency shall not require that a request contain more information than the requester's name and address and the information necessary to ascertain the records to which the requester desires access and the requester's right of access to the records.
rules.notes: Emitted as universal-access rule per contract. Caveat: where access or use is restricted under K.S.A. 45-221 or 45-230, subsection (c) permits requiring a written certification (see KS-0010); and the clause requires info establishing the requester's 'right of access,' so this is not a pure no-purpose regime. Same clause backs KS-0006.

rules.legal_concept: Agency may require a written request for inspection
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may require a written request for inspection of public records but shall not otherwise require a request in any particular form.
rules.trigger: Agency election
rules.source_language: A public agency may require a written request for inspection of public records but shall not otherwise require a request to be made in any particular form.
rules.notes: Writing is permissive, not mandatory statewide; the city fills in whether it requires writing. Second clause captured separately as KS-0005.

rules.atomic_rule: A public agency shall not require a request to be made in any particular form.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A public agency may require a written request for inspection of public records but shall not otherwise require a request to be made in any particular form.

rules.legal_concept: Limit on information the agency may require
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency shall not require that a request contain more than the requester's name and address, information necessary to ascertain the records desired, and the requester's right of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by subsection (c), a public agency shall not require that a request contain more information than the requester's name and address and the information necessary to ascertain the records to which the requester desires access and the requester's right of access to the records.

rules.legal_concept: Proof of identity may be required
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may require proof of identity of any person requesting access to a public record.
rules.trigger: Agency election
rules.source_language: A public agency may require proof of identity of any person requesting access to a public record.

rules.legal_concept: No denial for technicality; identifiable-records condition
rules.atomic_rule: No request shall be returned, delayed, or denied because of any technicality unless it is impossible to determine the records to which the requester desires access.
rules.trigger: Request received
rules.source_language: No request shall be returned, delayed or denied because of any technicality unless it is impossible to determine the records to which the requester desires access.
rules.notes: Carries the identifiable-records gate: duty may be excused only where it is impossible to determine the records sought.

rules.legal_concept: Written request and advance payment for copies
rules.atomic_rule: If copies are requested, the public agency may require a written request and advance payment of the prescribed fee.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for copies (as opposed to inspection)
rules.source_language: If copies are requested, the public agency may require a written request and advance payment of the prescribed fee.
rules.notes: Advance-payment aspect also carried by KS-0043 (K.S.A. 45-218(f)).

rules.legal_concept: Written certification when access or use is restricted
rules.atomic_rule: Where access to records or their permitted use is limited under K.S.A. 45-221 or 45-230, the agency may require the requester to certify in writing either a right of access or that the requester will not use/sell any list of names and addresses to sell property or services.
rules.trigger: Access to the records, or their permitted use, is limited under K.S.A. 45-221 or 45-230
rules.source_language: If access to public records of an agency or the purpose for which the records may be used is limited pursuant to K.S.A. 45-221 or 45-230, and amendments thereto, the agency may require a person requesting the records or information therein to provide written certification that: (1) The requester has a right of access to the records and the basis of that right; or (2) the requester does not intend to, and will not: (A) Use any list of names or addresses contained in or derived from the records or information for the purpose of selling or offering for sale any property or service to any person listed or to any person who resides at any address listed; or (B) sell, give or otherwise make available to any person any list of names or addresses contained in or derived from the records or information for the purpose of allowing that person to sell or offer for sale any property or service to any person listed or to any person who resides at any address listed.
rules.notes: Processing hook for the K.S.A. 45-230 list-sale prohibition. This certification is the software's branch point when names/addresses are involved.

rules.atomic_rule: Each public agency shall adopt procedures that provide full access, protect records, prevent excessive disruption, provide assistance and information, and ensure efficient and timely action on requests.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation)
rules.source_language: Each public agency shall adopt procedures to be followed in requesting access to and obtaining copies of public records, which procedures shall provide full access to public records, protect public records from damage and disorganization, prevent excessive disruption of the agency's essential functions, provide assistance and information upon request and ensure efficient and timely action in response to applications for inspection of public records.
rules.notes: 'Ensure efficient and timely action' is an undefined soft standard; not a numeric deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Agency must disclose procedure/custodian/fee information on request
rules.atomic_rule: Each public agency shall, upon request of any person, provide its principal office and office hours, the title and address of the official custodian and any ordinarily-available custodian, the fees charged, and the procedures for requesting records.
rules.trigger: Any person requests the information
rules.source_language: Each public agency shall provide, upon request of any person, the following information: (1) The principal office of the agency, its regular office hours and any additional hours established by the agency pursuant to subsection (c). (2) The title and address of the official custodian of the agency's records and of any other custodian who is ordinarily available to act on requests made at the location where the information is displayed. (3) The fees, if any, charged for access to or copies of the agency's records. (4) The procedures to be followed in requesting access to and obtaining copies of the agency's records, including procedures for giving notice of a desire to inspect or obtain copies of records during hours established by the agency pursuant to subsection (c).

rules.legal_concept: Non-custodian must redirect requester to the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: If the person to whom the request is directed is not the custodian, that person shall notify the requester and furnish the custodian's name and location, if known or readily ascertainable.
rules.trigger: Request directed to a person who is not the custodian of the requested record
rules.source_language: If the person to whom the request is directed is not the custodian of the public record requested, such person shall so notify the requester and shall furnish the name and location of the custodian of the public record, if known to or readily ascertainable by such person.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: drives routing to the correct custodian.

rules.atomic_rule: Each official custodian shall designate the persons necessary to carry out custodian duties and shall ensure a custodian is available during regular business hours.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation)
rules.source_language: Each official custodian of public records shall designate such persons as necessary to carry out the duties of custodian under this act and shall ensure that a custodian is available during regular business hours of the public agency to carry out such duties.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of custodian and official custodian
rules.atomic_rule: The 'official custodian' is any officer/employee responsible for maintaining public records (regardless of actual personal custody); 'custodian' includes any person the official custodian designates.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: (f) "Custodian" means the official custodian or any person designated by the official custodian to carry out the duties of custodian of this act. ... (j) "Official custodian" means any officer or employee of a public agency who is responsible for the maintenance of public records, regardless of whether such records are in the officer's or employee's actual personal custody and control.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on for routing (who must respond).

rules.legal_concept: Criminal justice records routed to originating agency
rules.atomic_rule: Except for multi-agency summary data or as otherwise provided by law, requests for records held in the KBI-maintained central/criminal-justice repositories shall be directed to the criminal justice agency from which the records originated.
rules.trigger: Request seeks records in the criminal justice information system repositories
rules.source_language: Except for requests of summary data compiled from information submitted by multiple criminal justice agencies or as otherwise provided by law, requests for records submitted to the central repository or any other repositories supporting the criminal justice information system that are maintained by the Kansas bureau of investigation pursuant to K.S.A. 22-4704 and 22-4705, and amendments thereto, shall be directed to the criminal justice agency from which the records originated.
rules.notes: Record-specific routing directive; relevant to municipal/local law enforcement requests.

rules.legal_concept: Asset seizure/forfeiture records routed to originating agency
rules.atomic_rule: Except for multi-agency summary data or as otherwise provided by law, requests for records in the KBI-maintained Kansas asset seizure and forfeiture repository shall be directed to the law enforcement agency from which the records originated.
rules.trigger: Request seeks records in the asset seizure and forfeiture repository
rules.source_language: Except for requests of summary data compiled from information submitted by multiple law enforcement agencies or as otherwise provided by law, requests for records submitted to the Kansas asset seizure and forfeiture repository that are maintained by the Kansas bureau of investigation pursuant to K.S.A. 60-4127, and amendments thereto, shall be directed to the law enforcement agency from which the records originated.

rules.atomic_rule: Requests for records defined as 'files' under K.S.A. 75-4379 submitted to a state or local law enforcement or governmental agency shall be directed to the agency that made, maintained, or kept such files.
rules.trigger: Request seeks records that are 'files' under K.S.A. 75-4379
rules.source_language: Requests for records defined as "files" pursuant to K.S.A. 75-4379, and amendments thereto, submitted to a state or local law enforcement agency or governmental agency shall be directed to the state or local law enforcement agency or governmental agency that made, maintained or kept such files, as required by K.S.A. 75-4379, and amendments thereto.

rules.legal_concept: ALPR data routed to owning agency
rules.atomic_rule: Requests for records containing captured license plate data or pertaining to the location of an automated license plate recognition system shall be directed to the agency that owns, leases, or contracts for the system.
rules.trigger: Request seeks captured license plate data or ALPR-location records
rules.source_language: Requests for records that contain captured license plate data or that pertain to the location of an automated license plate recognition system submitted to a state or local law enforcement agency or governmental agency shall be directed to the state or local law enforcement agency or governmental agency that owns, leases or contracts for the automated license plate recognition system.

rules.atomic_rule: 'Public agency' means the state or any political/taxing subdivision or any office, agency, or instrumentality thereof, or any other entity receiving or expending and supported in whole or part by public funds; with enumerated exclusions.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: (k)(1) "Public agency" means the state or any political or taxing subdivision of the state or any office, agency or instrumentality thereof, or any other entity receiving or expending and supported in whole or in part by the public funds appropriated by the state or by public funds of any political or taxing subdivision of the state.
rules.notes: Coverage gate: determines whether the entity (e.g., a municipality) is subject to KORA. Exclusions in (k)(2) not quoted in full here.

rules.atomic_rule: 'Public record' means any recorded information, regardless of form, characteristics, or location, that is made, maintained, or kept by, or is in the possession of, a public agency (with statutory exceptions).
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: (l)(1) "Public record" means any recorded information, regardless of form, characteristics or location, that is made, maintained or kept by or is in the possession of:
rules.notes: PARTIAL capture: only the lead-in of (l)(1) was quoted; subparagraphs and exclusions of (l) require manual verification of full text.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of business day for clock computation
rules.atomic_rule: 'Business day' means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or a holiday designated by the U.S. Congress, the Kansas legislature or governor, or the respective political subdivision.
rules.trigger: Any KORA deadline expressed in business days
rules.source_language: "Business day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or day designated as a holiday by the congress of the United States, by the legislature or governor of this state or by the respective political subdivision of this state.
rules.notes: Computation input for the three-business-day windows (KS-0026, KS-0030, KS-0042). Note political subdivisions may designate their own holidays.

rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect public records during the public agency's regular office hours and any additional hours established under K.S.A. 45-220.
rules.trigger: Request made in accordance with adopted procedures
rules.source_language: Upon request in accordance with procedures adopted under K.S.A. 45-220, any person may inspect public records during the regular office hours of the public agency and during any additional hours established by the public agency pursuant to K.S.A. 45-220.
rules.notes: The city supplies its actual office-hours value; the state sets the standard, not a number.

rules.legal_concept: Additional inspection hours and advance-notice cap
rules.atomic_rule: For business days without regular office hours, the agency shall establish reasonable inspection/copy hours; it may require prior notice, but such notice need not be in writing and cannot be required more than 24 hours in advance.
rules.trigger: Business day on which the agency does not maintain regular office hours
rules.source_language: A public agency shall establish, for business days when it does not maintain regular office hours, reasonable hours when persons may inspect and obtain copies of the agency's records. The public agency may require that any person desiring to inspect or obtain copies of the agency's records during such hours so notify the agency, but such notice shall not be required to be in writing and shall not be required to be given more than 24 hours prior to the hours established for inspection and obtaining copies.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: prior notice may not be required more than 24 hours before established hours
rules.notes: The 24-hour figure is a ceiling on how far in advance notice may be demanded, not a response deadline.

rules.legal_concept: No removal of original records without permission
rules.atomic_rule: No person shall remove original copies of public records from the office of any public agency without the written permission of the custodian.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks to remove original records
rules.source_language: No person shall removal* original copies of public records from the office of any public agency without the written permission of the custodian of the record.
rules.notes: Revisor's note states the word 'removal' should have been 'remove.' Quoted verbatim including the statutory typo.

rules.atomic_rule: Each request for access shall be acted upon as soon as possible, but not later than the end of the third business day following the date the request is received.
rules.trigger: Request for access received
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 3 business-days from date request is received (with soft 'as soon as possible' floor)
rules.source_language: Each request for access to a public record shall be acted upon as soon as possible, but not later than the end of the third business day following the date that the request is received.
rules.notes: One sentence bundles a soft 'as soon as possible' standard with a hard 3-business-day ceiling; captured as one atomic deadline. 'Acted upon' does not necessarily mean production complete (see KS-0027 delay explanation).

rules.legal_concept: Detailed delay explanation with date certain
rules.atomic_rule: If access is not granted immediately, the custodian shall give a detailed explanation of the cause for further delay and the place and earliest time and date the record will be available for inspection.
rules.trigger: Access not granted immediately upon acting on the request
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "earliest time and date that the record will be available" from delay notice
rules.source_language: If access to the public record is not granted immediately, the custodian shall give a detailed explanation of the cause for further delay and the place and earliest time and date that the record will be available for inspection.
rules.notes: Soft/date-certain standard set by the custodian, not a fixed statutory number; config home structural per soft-standard rule.

rules.legal_concept: Written statement of grounds furnished upon request
rules.atomic_rule: If the request for access is denied, the custodian shall provide, upon request, a written statement of the grounds for denial.
rules.trigger: Access denied AND requester asks for a written statement of grounds
rules.source_language: If the request for access is denied, the custodian shall provide, upon request, a written statement of the grounds for denial.
rules.notes: Distinctive Kansas feature: the written denial statement is owed only 'upon request,' not automatically.

rules.legal_concept: Denial statement must cite the specific legal provision
rules.atomic_rule: The written statement of denial shall cite the specific provision of law under which access is denied.
rules.trigger: Written statement of grounds for denial is furnished
rules.source_language: Such statement shall cite the specific provision of law under which access is denied and shall be furnished to the requester not later than the end of the third business day following the date that the request for the statement is received.

rules.legal_concept: Three-business-day deadline for written denial statement
rules.atomic_rule: The written statement of grounds for denial shall be furnished not later than the end of the third business day following the date the request for the statement is received.
rules.trigger: Requester's request for a written statement of grounds received
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 3 business-days from receipt of the request for the written statement
rules.source_language: Such statement shall cite the specific provision of law under which access is denied and shall be furnished to the requester not later than the end of the third business day following the date that the request for the statement is received.
rules.notes: Clock runs from receipt of the request FOR the statement, not from the original records request.

rules.legal_concept: Refusal for unreasonable burden or disruptive repeated requests
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may refuse access if a request places an unreasonable burden in producing records, or if the custodian has reason to believe repeated requests are intended to disrupt other essential functions; such refusal must be sustained by a preponderance of the evidence.
rules.trigger: Request places an unreasonable burden, or repeated requests believed intended to disrupt essential functions
rules.source_language: The custodian may refuse to provide access to a public record, or to permit inspection, if a request places an unreasonable burden in producing public records or if the custodian has reason to believe that repeated requests are intended to disrupt other essential functions of the public agency. However, refusal under this subsection must be sustained by preponderance of the evidence.
rules.notes: 'Unreasonable burden' is an undefined soft standard; agency bears preponderance burden to sustain. See AG Op. 1998-51.

rules.legal_concept: Separate/delete non-disclosable material and produce the rest
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains material not subject to disclosure, the agency shall separate or delete that material and make the disclosable remainder available; identifying portions of records pertaining to an identifiable individual shall be deleted and remaining disclosable portions produced.
rules.trigger: Requested record contains both disclosable and non-disclosable material
rules.source_language: If a public record contains material that is not subject to disclosure pursuant to this act, the public agency shall separate or delete such material and make available to the requester that material in the public record that is subject to disclosure pursuant to this act. If a public record is not subject to disclosure because it pertains to an identifiable individual, the public agency shall delete the identifying portions of the record and make available to the requester any remaining portions that are subject to disclosure pursuant to this act, unless the request is for a record pertaining to a specific individual or to such a limited group of individuals that the individuals' identities are reasonably ascertainable, the public agency shall not be required to disclose those portions of the record that pertain to such individual or individuals.
rules.notes: Includes a limited-group exception where individuals' identities are reasonably ascertainable.

rules.atomic_rule: Except where fees are prescribed by statute or subsection (h) applies, each public agency may prescribe reasonable fees for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to enumerated limits.
rules.trigger: Agency prescribes a fee
rules.source_language: Except as provided by subsection (h) or where fees for inspection or for copies of a public record are prescribed by statute, each public agency may prescribe reasonable fees for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to the following:
rules.notes: Umbrella soft-standard ('reasonable'); the actual-cost ceiling is KS-0034. The city supplies the value under the reasonableness standard.

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee capped at actual cost including staff time
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for copies shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available.
rules.trigger: Agency charges for copies of records
rules.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records.
rules.notes: Unlike states that bar search/review labor, Kansas expressly permits charging staff time and review/redaction cost (KS-0035). Excludes non-attributable incidental costs.

rules.legal_concept: Review and redaction costs chargeable; incidentals excluded
rules.atomic_rule: Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs not attributable to furnishing the requested records.
rules.trigger: Records require review/redaction before production
rules.source_language: Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records.

rules.legal_concept: Computer-access fees limited to computer-service cost
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for providing access to records maintained on computer facilities shall include only the cost of any computer services, including staff time required.
rules.trigger: Access to records maintained on computer facilities
rules.source_language: In the case of fees for providing access to records maintained on computer facilities, the fees shall include only the cost of any computer services, including staff time required.

rules.legal_concept: Good-faith use of lowest-cost staff category
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency incurs staff-time costs, it shall use in good faith the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary to provide access or furnish copies.
rules.trigger: Agency incurs staff-time cost to fulfill the request
rules.source_language: If the public agency incurs costs for staff time to provide access to or furnish copies of public records, the agency shall use in good faith the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary to provide access to or furnish copies of public records.

rules.legal_concept: Staff-time charges based on salary/wage, excluding benefits
rules.atomic_rule: Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage and shall not include the costs of employee benefits.
rules.trigger: Agency charges for staff time
rules.source_language: Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage. Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits.

rules.legal_concept: Itemized statement of costs on request
rules.atomic_rule: Upon request, the agency shall provide an itemized statement of costs charged to the requester, including the hourly rates for each employee involved and an itemized list of any other fees.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for an itemized statement of costs
rules.source_language: Upon request, a public agency shall provide to the person requesting access to or copies of public records pursuant to this section an itemized statement of costs incurred by the public agency and charged to such requester. Such itemized statement shall include, but not be limited to, the hourly rates charged for each employee involved in making the requested records available and an itemized list of any other fees charged to provide access to or furnish copies of the requested records.

rules.legal_concept: Cost of copying at other facilities and supervision fee
rules.atomic_rule: If it is necessary to use other facilities for copying, the requester shall pay that cost; the agency may also charge the same supervision fee as for furnishing copies under subsection (c).
rules.trigger: Copying cannot practicably be done where records are kept, so other facilities are used
rules.source_language: If it is necessary to use other facilities for copying, the cost thereof shall be paid by the person desiring a copy of the records. In addition, the public agency may charge the same fee for the services rendered in supervising the copying as for furnishing copies under subsection (c) and may establish a reasonable schedule of times for making copies at other facilities.

rules.atomic_rule: When staff time to respond will exceed five hours, or estimated actual staff-time cost exceeds $200, the agency shall make reasonable efforts to contact the requester and engage in interactive communication about mitigating costs; the requester is not obligated to mitigate.
rules.trigger: Staff time to respond will exceed 5 hours OR estimated actual staff-time cost exceeds $200
rules.source_language: When the staff time needed to respond to a records request will exceed five hours or the estimated actual cost for staff time needed to fill the request exceeds $200, the public agency shall make reasonable efforts to contact the requester and engage in interactive communication about mitigating costs to fill the request. The requester is not obligated to mitigate costs.
rules.notes: Added by L. 2025, ch. 89 (eff. 2025-07-01). Thresholds (5 hours / $200) are fixed statutory triggers. 'Reasonable efforts to contact' defined in (e)(3) as contacting via the means the requester provided.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed withdrawal on failure to respond to cost-mitigation contact
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency has made reasonable efforts to contact the requester under subsection (e) and the requester fails to respond by the end of the third business day, the request is deemed withdrawn until the requester makes subsequent contact.
rules.trigger: Agency made reasonable-efforts contact AND requester fails to respond by end of third business day
rules.clock_spec: terminal: deemed withdrawn if no requester response by end of 3rd business day after the agency's reasonable-efforts contact
rules.source_language: If a public agency has made reasonable efforts to contact the requester pursuant to this section and the requester has failed to respond by the end of the third business day, the records request will be deemed to be withdrawn until a subsequent contact has been made by the requester to the public agency.
rules.notes: Added by L. 2025, ch. 89. Deemed-withdrawn is a state the request enters (reversible on subsequent requester contact); config home structural. Terminal clock triggered by requester silence.

rules.legal_concept: Advance payment of fees may be required
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may charge and require advance payment of a fee for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to K.S.A. 45-219.
rules.trigger: Agency elects to charge a fee
rules.source_language: A public agency may charge and require advance payment of a fee for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to K.S.A. 45-219.
rules.notes: Also stated in K.S.A. 45-219(a) for copies (see KS-0009).

rules.legal_concept: No duty to copy audio/visual media (with exceptions)
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency is not required to provide copies of tapes, discs, video, film, pictures, slides, graphics, illustrations, or similar audio/visual items unless they were shown/played to a public meeting of the governing body; and need not provide items copyrighted by another.
rules.trigger: Request seeks copies of audio/visual items or devices
rules.source_language: A public agency shall not be required to provide copies of radio or recording tapes or discs, video tapes or films, pictures, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items or devices, unless such items or devices were shown or played to a public meeting of the governing body thereof, except that the public agency shall not be required to provide such items or devices that are copyrighted by a person other than the public agency.

rules.legal_concept: Copies made under custodian supervision, in place where kept
rules.atomic_rule: Copies shall be made while records are in the custodian's possession/custody/control and under the custodian's supervision; whenever practicable, copies shall be made where the records are kept, and if not practicable the custodian shall allow arrangements for other facilities.
rules.trigger: Copies of records are to be made
rules.source_language: Copies of public records shall be made while the records are in the possession, custody and control of the custodian or a person designated by the custodian and shall be made under the supervision of such custodian or person. Whenever practicable, copies shall be made in the place where the records are kept. If it is not practicable to do so, the custodian shall allow arrangements to be made for use of other facilities.

rules.legal_concept: Copy must be provided in the format the agency maintains it
rules.atomic_rule: K.S.A. 45-219(a) requires a public agency, upon request, to provide a copy of a public record in the format in which the agency maintains that record.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a copy in the format the agency maintains the record
rules.source_language: The plain language of K.S.A. 45-219(a) requires a public agency, upon request, to provide a copy of a public record in the format in which the agency maintains that record.
rules.source_authority: Roe v. Phillips Cnty. Hosp., 317 Kan. 1, 522 P.3d 277 (2023)
rules.notes: Judicially established rule interpreting K.S.A. 45-219(a). Source language quoted from the statute's case annotation on the Revisor site.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to allow requester's device to be attached to agency computer
rules.atomic_rule: Nothing in the act requires an agency to make electronic copies by allowing a person to attach an electronic device provided by that person to the agency's computer or other electronic device.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks to attach their own electronic device to obtain copies
rules.source_language: Nothing in the open records act shall require a public agency to electronically make copies of public records by allowing a person to obtain copies of a public record by inserting, connecting or otherwise attaching an electronic device provided by such person to the computer or other electronic device of the public agency.

rules.atomic_rule: The district court of any county where the records are located has jurisdiction to enforce the act by injunction, mandamus, declaratory judgment, or other appropriate order, in an action brought by any person, the attorney general, or a county or district attorney.
rules.trigger: Person, AG, or county/district attorney brings an enforcement action
rules.source_language: The district court of any county in which public records are located shall have jurisdiction to enforce the purposes of this act with respect to such records, by injunction, mandamus, declaratory judgment or other appropriate order, in an action brought by any person, the attorney general or a county or district attorney.
rules.notes: Judicial path only; namespaced appeal.judicial. The court may also require a defendant to complete AG-approved training (remedy detail excluded).

rules.legal_concept: De novo review and in camera inspection
rules.atomic_rule: In any enforcement action the court shall determine the matter de novo and may, on its own or a party's motion, view the records in controversy in camera before deciding.
rules.trigger: KORA enforcement action pending
rules.source_language: In any action hereunder, the court shall determine the matter de novo. The court on its own motion, or on motion of either party, may view the records in controversy in camera before reaching a decision.

rules.legal_concept: Burden of proof on the public agency
rules.atomic_rule: In any enforcement action (or action under K.S.A. 45-251), the burden of proof is on the public agency to sustain its action.
rules.trigger: KORA enforcement action pending
rules.source_language: In any action hereunder, or under K.S.A. 45-251, and amendments thereto, the burden of proof shall be on the public agency to sustain its action.

material_negatives.note: KORA sets no fixed extension mechanism. Beyond the three-business-day action deadline (KS-0026), the only 'extension' path is the custodian's 'detailed explanation of the cause for further delay' with an earliest date of availability (KS-0027) — a soft standard, not a numeric extension with enumerated grounds.

No explicit statutory 'silence = denial / deemed denial' trigger. KORA imposes the three-business-day action deadline and provides judicial enforcement, but does not state that non-response after N days constitutes a denial. (The 2025 fee-mitigation provision creates a deemed WITHDRAWAL for requester non-response — KS-0042 — which is not a deemed denial.)

No general internal/administrative appeal stage for municipal requests. The only administrative-review path in KORA is a fee-reasonableness appeal to the Secretary of Administration under K.S.A. 45-219(d), and that is limited to records within the state EXECUTIVE BRANCH — inapplicable to municipal requests. Municipal recourse is judicial (K.S.A. 45-222).

No statewide fixed per-page copy rate for general municipal records. Copy fees are governed by 'reasonable' and 'actual cost' standards (KS-0033, KS-0034), with the city supplying the operative value; there is no statutory cents-per-page cap in the open records act.
KORA contains no public-interest or indigency fee-waiver provision.

No separate commercial-purpose fee tier. KORA does not define 'commercial purpose' or set a higher rate for commercial requesters; it instead restricts sale/use of name-and-address lists (K.S.A. 45-230) and permits a non-sale certification (KS-0010).

No explicit statutory rule that inspection is free of charge. K.S.A. 45-218(f) permits charging a fee for 'providing access to' records; inspection during office hours is provided but the act does not expressly bar an access fee for inspection.
KORA contains no request-triggered preservation or litigation-hold provision; records retention/destruction is governed outside the open records act.

No express clarification-request mechanism or clarification clock. The nearest provisions are the requirement that a request contain enough information to ascertain the records sought and the 'impossible to determine the records' technicality exception (KS-0008), plus the 2025 cost-mitigation interactive communication (KS-0041).
Oral requests are not guaranteed; the agency 'may require a written request' (KS-0004). No statutory duty to accept oral requests.

No general statutory requester right to choose the electronic format/medium. The duty established judicially (KS-0046) is to provide a copy in the format the agency MAINTAINS the record, and the agency need not allow requester devices to be attached (KS-0047).

structural_branches.description: Deemed-withdrawal state (KS-0042): after a triggered cost-mitigation contact (KS-0041), requester silence for three business days moves the request into a 'deemed withdrawn' state, reversible only on subsequent requester contact. A Kansas-specific path added by L. 2025, ch. 89.
Interactive cost-mitigation conference stage (KS-0041): crossing the 5-hour / $200 staff-time threshold forces a mandatory contact-and-confer step before the request proceeds.

Two-step denial path (KS-0028 to KS-0030): denial itself is communicated within the general 3-business-day window, but the written, provision-citing statement of grounds is owed only 'upon request,' and its own separate 3-business-day clock runs from receipt of that follow-up request.

Restricted-access certification gate (KS-0010): where access or use is limited under K.S.A. 45-221 or 45-230, the request branches to require a written right-of-access or non-sale certification before production.

Record-type routing forks (KS-0016 to KS-0019): criminal-justice-repository records, asset-seizure-repository records, 'files' under K.S.A. 75-4379, and ALPR data are each statutorily routed to the originating/owning agency rather than the receiving agency.
Non-custodian redirect (KS-0013): a non-custodian recipient must route the requester to the named custodian's location.

Judicial enforcement path (KS-0048 to KS-0050): the sole review route for municipal requests is a de novo district-court action with in camera inspection and the burden of proof on the agency; there is no municipal administrative-appeal stage.

rules.legal_concept: Right of any person to inspect and copy public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect and copy the public records of any public agency during the agency's regular business hours.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of access)
rules.source_language: Any person may inspect and copy the public records of any public agency during the regular business hours of the agency, except as provided in section 4 of this chapter.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key. 'Except as provided in section 4' points to the enumerated exemptions.

rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may not deny a request because the requester refuses to state the purpose of the request, unless another applicable statute requires it.
rules.trigger: Requester declines to state a purpose
rules.source_language: No request may be denied because the person making the request refuses to state the purpose of the request, unless such condition is required by other applicable statute.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key.

rules.atomic_rule: The right to inspect and copy public records extends to any person; the Act imposes no residency or citizenship qualification.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The Access to Public Records Act extends the right to 'any person' and contains no residency or citizenship qualification on the right to request records.
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule per universal-access symmetry (never a material negative). Paraphrase: the Act states 'any person' affirmatively; the absence of a residency requirement is not stated as a distinct operative clause. Manual verification of any residency-adjacent limits recommended.

rules.atomic_rule: A request must identify with reasonable particularity the record being requested for the agency's duty to attach.
rules.trigger: A request is submitted
rules.source_language: A request for inspection or copying must identify with reasonable particularity the record being requested and, at the discretion of the agency, be in writing on or in a form provided by the agency.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable particularity' is an undefined standard - not converted to a numeric threshold. Same source clause as IN-0005 (split into the particularity requirement and the writing/form discretion).

rules.legal_concept: Writing / agency form at agency discretion
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may, at its discretion, require a request to be in writing on or in a form provided by the agency.
rules.trigger: Agency elects to require writing/its form
rules.source_language: A request for inspection or copying must identify with reasonable particularity the record being requested and, at the discretion of the agency, be in writing on or in a form provided by the agency.
rules.notes: Writing/form is permissive at the agency's option, not a fixed statutory requirement; in-person and telephone (oral) requests are contemplated by the 24-hour response trigger in § 5-14-3-9.

rules.atomic_rule: Inspection and copying are available during the agency's regular business hours.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Any person may inspect and copy the public records of any public agency during the regular business hours of the agency, except as provided in section 4 of this chapter.
rules.notes: The city/agency supplies the actual hours under the soft standard 'regular business hours.'

rules.legal_concept: 24-hour deemed-denial window (in person / telephone / enhanced access)
rules.atomic_rule: For a request made in person, by telephone, or for enhanced access, a denial is deemed to occur when 24 hours elapse after an agency employee refuses to permit inspection and copying.
rules.trigger: Request made in person, by telephone, or for enhanced access; agency does not permit inspection/copying
rules.clock_spec: terminal: denial deemed at 24 hours after an agency employee's refusal to permit inspection/copying (in-person, telephone, or enhanced-access requests)
rules.source_language: A denial of disclosure occurs when the person making the request is physically present in the office of the public agency, makes the request by telephone, or requests enhanced access to a document and ... twenty-four (24) hours elapse after any employee of the public agency refuses to permit inspection and copying of a public record when a request has been made.
rules.notes: This window defines when a constructive denial occurs (enabling PAC complaint / suit), not a production deadline. Constraint fixed by statute; the city cannot alter it.

rules.atomic_rule: For a request received by mail or facsimile, a denial of disclosure does not occur until seven days elapse from the date the agency receives the request.
rules.trigger: Request received by mail or facsimile
rules.clock_spec: terminal: denial deemed 7 days from the date the public agency receives a mailed or faxed request
rules.source_language: If a person requests by mail or by facsimile a copy or copies of a public record, a denial of disclosure does not occur until seven (7) days have elapsed from the date the public agency receives the request.
rules.notes: Deemed-denial trigger for mailed/faxed requests. Not a production deadline; constraint fixed by statute.

rules.atomic_rule: Agency silence/refusal for the applicable statutory window is deemed a denial of disclosure, moving the request into a denied state.
rules.trigger: Applicable 24-hour or 7-day window elapses without disclosure
rules.clock_spec: terminal: request enters denied state upon expiry of the applicable § 5-14-3-9 window
rules.source_language: A denial of disclosure by a public agency occurs when ... twenty-four (24) hours elapse after any employee of the public agency refuses to permit inspection and copying ... [or, for mail/fax requests,] seven (7) days have elapsed from the date the public agency receives the request.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver (deemed/constructive denial trigger). The terminal event that gives the requester standing to complain to the PAC or sue.

rules.atomic_rule: After a proper request, the agency must produce copies or permit copying within a reasonable time.
rules.trigger: A valid request is received
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "reasonable time" from request receipt
rules.source_language: Within a reasonable time after the request is received, the public agency must either provide copies, allow copying on the agency's equipment, or allow the person to copy on the person's own equipment.
rules.notes: Soft standard - not a numeric deadline; config_home=structural per soft-deadline rule. Paraphrase: the exact operative clause could not be captured verbatim from an official page. Indiana has no fixed statutory production deadline apart from the § 5-14-3-9 deemed-denial windows. Manual verification recommended.

rules.legal_concept: Separation of disclosable from nondisclosable material
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both disclosable and nondisclosable information, the agency must separate the disclosable material and make it available for inspection and copying.
rules.trigger: Requested record contains a mix of disclosable and nondisclosable information
rules.source_language: If a public record contains disclosable and nondisclosable information, the public agency shall, upon receipt of a request under this chapter, separate the material that may be disclosed and make it available for inspection and copying.

rules.legal_concept: Direct cost of reprogramming to separate disclosable data
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge the requester the agency's direct cost of reprogramming a computer system where reprogramming is required to separate disclosable from nondisclosable information stored electronically.
rules.trigger: Disclosable info is on a computer/analogous system AND reprogramming is required to segregate it
rules.source_language: A public agency may charge a person who makes a request for disclosable information the agency's direct cost of reprogramming a computer system if: (1) the disclosable information is stored on a computer tape, computer disc, or a similar or analogous record system; and (2) the public agency is required to reprogram the computer system to separate the disclosable information from nondisclosable information.
rules.notes: Charge capped at 'direct cost' (ceiling). Attaches to the segregability duty in IN-0011.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to reprogram for enhanced access
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to reprogram a computer system to provide enhanced access or access to a governmental entity by an electronic device.
rules.trigger: Request would require reprogramming for enhanced access / electronic-device access
rules.source_language: A public agency is not required to reprogram a computer system to provide: (1) enhanced access; or (2) access to a governmental entity by an electronic device.

rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may not charge any fee to inspect a public record.
rules.trigger: Requester inspects (does not copy)
rules.source_language: A public agency may not charge any fee under this chapter for the following: (1) To inspect a public record.
rules.notes: Fixed at $0 for inspection.

rules.legal_concept: Copying fee ceiling (greater of per-page rate or actual cost)
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of ten cents ($0.10) per non-color page or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per color page, or the agency's actual cost.
rules.trigger: Requester obtains paper copies
rules.source_language: The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of: (1) ten cents ($0.10) per page for copies that are not color copies or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for color copies; or (2) the actual cost to the agency.
rules.notes: Ceiling. For local agencies the copying fee schedule is established by the fiscal body (see IN-0019). Same concept as a fixed-25-cent rule elsewhere per constraint-basis guidance.

rules.atomic_rule: The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document.
rules.trigger: Requester requests a certified copy
rules.source_language: The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document.
rules.notes: Ceiling per document.

rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge a fee for providing an electronic map based upon a reasonable percentage of the agency's direct cost of maintaining, upgrading, and enhancing the electronic map.
rules.trigger: Request is for an electronic map
rules.source_language: A public agency may charge a fee, uniform to all purchasers, for providing an electronic map that is based upon a reasonable percentage of the agency's direct cost of maintaining, upgrading, and enhancing the electronic map.
rules.notes: Special record type (electronic map) with a distinct fee basis; ceiling tied to a reasonable percentage of direct cost.

rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge any reasonable fee agreed on in an enhanced-access contract under section 3.5 for providing enhanced access to public records.
rules.trigger: Access is provided via an enhanced-access contract under § 5-14-3-3.5
rules.source_language: A public agency may charge any reasonable fee agreed on in the contract under section 3.5 of this chapter for providing enhanced access to public records.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable fee agreed on in the contract' - no statutory number; soft-standard, contract-set.

rules.legal_concept: Copying fee schedule set by fiscal body
rules.atomic_rule: For a local public agency, the fiscal body of the political subdivision establishes the copying fee schedule by ordinance, and the fee must be uniform.
rules.trigger: Local agency sets copy fees
rules.source_language: The fiscal body (as defined in IC 36-1-2-6) of the political subdivision shall establish a fee schedule for the certification or copying of documents ... The fee for copying documents may not exceed [the statutory ceiling].
rules.notes: Structural: the operative-value ceiling lives in IN-0015; this row is the requirement that a local fiscal body (not the records custodian) set the schedule. Paraphrase - exact subsection text not captured verbatim; verify subsection lettering and the uniformity clause.

rules.atomic_rule: A denial made in writing (or by facsimile) must include a statement of the specific exemption(s) authorizing the withholding and the name and title/position of the person responsible for the denial.
rules.trigger: Agency denies a written request in writing or by facsimile
rules.source_language: A denial of a request that is made in writing or by facsimile must be in writing and must include: (1) a statement of the specific exemption or exemptions authorizing the withholding of all or part of the public record; and (2) the name and the title or position of the person responsible for the denial.
rules.notes: Conjunctive contents kept in one row. Written-denial duty attaches only when the request itself was in writing or by facsimile.

rules.legal_concept: Formal complaint to the Public Access Counselor
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access may file a formal complaint with the Public Access Counselor, invoking an administrative-review path.
rules.trigger: A denial (actual or deemed) has occurred
rules.source_language: A person or a public agency that chooses to file a formal complaint with the counselor must file the complaint not later than thirty (30) days after ... the denial.
rules.notes: Administrative-review branch (namespaced appeal.administrative). The PAC issues a non-binding advisory opinion.

rules.legal_concept: 30-day deadline to file a PAC complaint
rules.atomic_rule: A formal complaint to the Public Access Counselor must be filed not later than 30 days after the denial.
rules.trigger: Denial occurs (or, if the denial is in writing, the date of the written denial)
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from the denial
rules.source_language: A person or a public agency that chooses to file a formal complaint with the counselor must file the complaint not later than thirty (30) days after ... the denial.
rules.notes: Fixed statutory window. Exact start-event wording (date of denial vs. date requester notified) should be confirmed against full subsection text.

rules.atomic_rule: The Public Access Counselor must issue an advisory opinion on the complaint not later than 30 days after the complaint is filed.
rules.trigger: A formal complaint is filed with the counselor
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from the complaint filing date
rules.source_language: The counselor shall issue an advisory opinion on the complaint not later than thirty (30) days after the complaint is filed.
rules.notes: Section 10 of the chapter provides an exception extending this deadline (text not captured; flag for later pass).

rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access may file an action in the circuit or superior court of the county where the denial occurred to compel the agency to permit inspection and copying.
rules.trigger: A denial of access has occurred
rules.source_language: A person who has been denied the right to inspect or copy a public record by a public agency may file an action in the circuit or superior court of the county in which the denial occurred to compel the public agency to permit the person to inspect and copy the public record.
rules.notes: Judicial-enforcement branch (namespaced appeal.judicial). Venue = county of denial.

rules.legal_concept: De novo review; burden on the agency
rules.atomic_rule: In an enforcement action the court reviews the matter de novo, and the burden of proof is on the public agency to sustain its denial.
rules.trigger: Enforcement action is filed
rules.source_language: The court shall determine the matter de novo, with the burden of proof on the public agency to sustain its denial.

rules.legal_concept: Liberal construction; doubt resolved for disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: The Act is to be liberally construed to implement its policy of full access; provisions are read in favor of disclosure.
rules.trigger: None stated (interpretive default)
rules.source_language: This chapter shall be liberally construed to implement this policy and place the burden of proof for the nondisclosure of a public record on the public agency that would deny access to the record and not on the person seeking to inspect and copy the public record.
rules.notes: Policy section that drives the disclosure default and burden allocation (passes inclusion test as it governs classification/denial defaults). Paraphrase - operative clause not captured verbatim from an official page; verify exact wording.

rules.atomic_rule: 'Commercial purpose' is defined by statute and, where it applies, drives fee treatment and the list-disclosure restriction.
rules.trigger: Request is for a commercial purpose
rules.source_language: 'Commercial purpose' is defined at IC 5-14-3-2 (definition not captured verbatim this pass).
rules.notes: Kept as a branch-driving definition (software branches on commercial purpose for fees / list restrictions). Exact definitional text could not be reproduced verbatim - manual verification required.

rules.legal_concept: Restriction on disclosure of name/address lists for commercial or political purposes
rules.atomic_rule: Enumerated lists (e.g., of names and addresses) may not be disclosed to any individual/entity for political purposes, nor to commercial entities for commercial purposes.
rules.trigger: Request seeks a covered list for a commercial or political purpose
rules.source_language: [Enumerated lists] may not be disclosed by public agencies to any individual or entity for political purposes ... [nor] to commercial entities for commercial purposes ... and may not be used ... for commercial purposes.
rules.notes: Blocks an action (disclosure) - passes inclusion test. Source language stitched from verbatim fragments; the precise enumeration of covered lists should be confirmed against full § 5-14-3-3.

rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may (but need not) permit a person to inspect and copy records through enhanced access under a contract described in section 3.5.
rules.trigger: Agency elects to offer enhanced access
rules.source_language: A public agency may or may not permit a person to inspect and copy through the use of enhanced access public records containing information owned by or entrusted to the public agency.
rules.notes: Optional enhanced-access path; fee governed by IN-0018.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic or paper copy at requester's option
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency shall provide an electronic copy or a paper copy of a public record at the option of the person making the request.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies electronic or paper format
rules.source_language: A public agency shall provide an electronic copy or a paper copy of a public record, at the option of the person making the request.
rules.notes: Format-choice belongs to the requester (subject to the agency actually maintaining the record in a given medium).

rules.legal_concept: Municipal/local entities are covered public agencies
rules.atomic_rule: 'Public agency' includes county, township, school, city, and town entities and other political subdivisions, so municipal records are within the Act.
rules.trigger: Request directed to a municipal/local government entity
rules.source_language: 'Public agency' means ... any ... county, township, school corporation, city, or town, or any other separate local governmental entity ... (definition summarized; full enumeration at IC 5-14-3-2).
rules.notes: Confirms municipal coverage (drives whether the platform handles the request at all). Paraphrase of a multi-clause definition - verify full enumeration.

structural_branches.description: Public Access Counselor formal-complaint path (IC 5-14-5): requester files a complaint within 30 days; PAC issues a non-binding advisory opinion within 30 days. A distinct administrative-review stage the engine must express.
Court action under IC 5-14-3-9(e) in the circuit/superior court of the county of denial to compel access; reviewed de novo with the burden on the agency.
Constructive denial: request moves to a denied state when the applicable 24-hour (in-person/phone/enhanced-access) or 7-day (mail/fax) window elapses - a channel-dependent terminal branch.
When a record is mixed, the agency must separate disclosable material and produce it; may branch to a reprogramming-cost charge for electronic separation (IC 5-14-3-6).
Optional enhanced-access path via a section-3.5 contract with its own contract-set fee - a fork the engine must support but need not require.
Liberal-construction / burden-on-agency default (IC 5-14-3-1) that governs how ambiguous classification and denial decisions resolve.

material_negatives.note: Indiana sets NO fixed statutory production/response deadline. The only statutory clocks are the § 5-14-3-9 deemed-denial windows (24 hours / 7 days) and a soft 'reasonable time' standard for production. Absence of a found fixed window is not proof none exists in a special-record statute.
No statutory requirement that the agency send an acknowledgment or an estimated completion date. (The deemed-denial windows substitute for an affirmative-acknowledgment duty.)
No explicit statutory clarification procedure or clarification clock; 'reasonable particularity' gates the duty but the Act does not codify a confer-to-narrow step or a nonresponse-abandonment clock.
No statutory extension/unusual-circumstances mechanism to lengthen a response window (there is no fixed window to extend).
APRA does not require agencies to designate or publicly identify a public-records/FOIA officer; it only requires a written denial to name the person responsible for the denial (IN-0020).
No statutory abandonment/withdrawal rule for a requester who fails to inspect, pay, or respond to a cost estimate.
No explicit statutory authorization to require a deposit or advance full payment before producing standard copies (agencies may set fee schedules; advance-payment practice was not found in statute).

Statute caps copy charges at per-page/actual cost and bars any inspection fee, but does not expressly address (bar or allow) search/review/labor charges for standard copies; treat as unresolved rather than assume either way.
No express statutory 'no duty to create a new record' provision found (contrast the reprogramming provisions in § 5-14-3-6, which address separation, not creation).

No statutory tolling of a response clock while awaiting a requester's answer to clarification/estimate (consistent with there being no fixed response clock). Any tolling of the 30-day PAC-complaint window during an informal inquiry (IC 5-14-5) was not captured verbatim and is flagged for a later pass.

rules.legal_concept: Public right of access to public records
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer must permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record to any requestor, without limiting access to a class of persons.
rules.trigger: A person submits a request for a public record.
rules.source_language: A records access officer appointed pursuant to section 6A, or a designee, shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record as defined in clause twenty-sixth of section 7 of chapter 4, or any segregable portion of a public record, not later than 10 business days following the receipt of the request
rules.notes: The statute grants access without any requester-class limitation (no residency, citizenship, or standing condition). Emitted as the shared universal-access key per cross-state symmetry.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship condition on access
rules.atomic_rule: Access to public records is not conditioned on the requestor's residency or citizenship; any person may request regardless of state of residence.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: A records access officer appointed pursuant to section 6A, or a designee, shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record ... not later than 10 business days following the receipt of the request, provided that: (i) the request reasonably describes the public record sought; (ii) the public record is within the possession, custody or control of the agency or municipality ...; and (iii) the records access officer receives payment of a reasonable fee
rules.notes: Derived from the ABSENCE of any residency condition in the statutory preconditions (which are limited to description, custody, and fee). is_paraphrase=true because it is an inference from absence, not a verbatim clause. Emitted as a rule with the shared key per universal-access symmetry rather than as a material negative.

rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may not require the requester to state the purpose of a request, except to determine a commercial purpose or to rule on a fee-waiver request.
rules.trigger: A person submits a request; RAO seeks to condition it on purpose.
rules.source_language: a records access officer may not require the requester to specify the purpose for a request, except to determine whether the records are requested for a commercial purpose or whether to grant a request for a fee waiver
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel at 950 CMR 32.06(1)(h), which adds a third exception for records that may be exempt under M.G.L. c. 4, § 7(26)(n).

rules.atomic_rule: 'Commercial purpose' means the sale/resale of a record or use of its information to advance the requester's strategic business interests for profit, excluding news, citizen oversight, and academic/scientific/journalistic/public research.
rules.trigger: RAO must classify a request to set fee basis or evaluate a fee-waiver/excess-fee petition.
rules.source_language: as used in this section ''commercial purpose'' shall mean the sale or resale of any portion of the public record or the use of information from the public record to advance the requester's strategic business interests in a manner that the requester can reasonably expect to make a profit, and shall not include gathering or reporting news or gathering information to promote citizen oversight or further the understanding of the operation or activities of government or for academic, scientific, journalistic or public research or education
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on: drives fee basis and eligibility for excess-fee/waiver treatment.

rules.atomic_rule: A valid request must reasonably describe the public record sought so the RAO can identify and locate it.
rules.trigger: A person submits a request.
rules.source_language: provided that: (i) the request reasonably describes the public record sought
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.06(1)(b). Gates whether the time clock starts (see MA-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Record within possession, custody or control
rules.atomic_rule: The duty to produce applies only where the record is within the possession, custody, or control of the agency or municipality the RAO serves.
rules.trigger: A request is received.
rules.source_language: (ii) the public record is within the possession, custody or control of the agency or municipality that the records access officer serves
rules.notes: Gates routing: records not in custody trigger the written-response identification duty in § 10(b)(ii)-(iii).

rules.atomic_rule: A request may be delivered by hand, by first class mail to the RAO's business address, or by electronic mail to the posted address (regulations add facsimile if the custodian has fax access).
rules.trigger: A person elects a delivery method.
rules.source_language: A request for public records may be delivered to the records access officer by hand or via first class mail at the record officer's business address, or via electronic mail to the address posted by the agency or municipality that the records access officer serves.
rules.notes: Regulation 950 CMR 32.06(1)(c) adds delivery by facsimile if the custodian has facsimile access.

rules.atomic_rule: Requests may be made orally in person to a records access officer or custodian; telephone requests may be accepted at the RAO's discretion.
rules.trigger: A person makes an oral request.
rules.source_language: requests for public records may be made orally in person to a records access officer or custodian or may be written. Telephone requests may be accepted at the discretion of the records access officer.
rules.notes: An oral request is valid but cannot be the basis of an administrative appeal (see MA-0064). Clock for oral request begins the day it was made.

rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer shall not require requesters to use a particular form, though optional forms may be made available.
rules.trigger: A person submits a request without using an agency form.
rules.source_language: a records access officer shall not require a particular form be used by requesters, but may make forms available for requesters.

rules.atomic_rule: Each agency and municipality must designate one or more employees as records access officers to coordinate and respond to public-records requests.
rules.trigger: None stated (ongoing structural obligation).
rules.source_language: Each agency and municipality shall designate 1 or more employees as records access officers.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: lives under officer-designation but drives who-must-respond / routing.

rules.legal_concept: Municipal clerk as records access officer
rules.atomic_rule: In a municipality, the municipal clerk (or the clerk's designees, or any designee the chief executive officer appoints) serves as records access officer.
rules.trigger: Municipal context.
rules.source_language: In a municipality, the municipal clerk, or the clerk's designees, or any designee of a municipality that the chief executive officer of the municipality may appoint, shall serve as records access officers.
rules.notes: Municipal-specific routing default.

rules.atomic_rule: If sought records are not within its possession, custody, or control, the written response must identify those records and identify the agency or municipality that may possess them, if known.
rules.trigger: Requested records are not within the responding entity's custody.
rules.source_language: (ii) identify any public records or categories of public records sought that are not within the possession, custody, or control of the agency or municipality that the records access officer serves; (iii) identify the agency or municipality that may be in possession, custody or control of the public record sought, if known;
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver routing rule; component of the § 10(b) written response.

rules.atomic_rule: 'Business day' means Monday through Friday, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, legal holidays, and weekdays when the custodian's office is unexpectedly closed.
rules.trigger: Any deadline computation in business days.
rules.source_language: Business Day. Monday through Friday. Business day does not include Saturdays, Sundays, legal holidays, or other weekdays where a custodian's office is closed
rules.notes: Governs the unit for all 'business day' deadlines in c. 66 § 10 and the regulations.

rules.atomic_rule: For a written request, time computation begins on the first business day following the date of receipt; an oral request is deemed received the day it was made.
rules.trigger: A valid request is received.
rules.clock_spec: start event: first business day following receipt (written) / day made (oral)
rules.source_language: Unless otherwise provided, the computation of time referred to in 950 CMR 32.00 shall begin with the first business day following the date of receipt of any request, regardless of physical form. The computation of time for an oral request shall begin with the day the oral request was made to the custodian.
rules.notes: Defines the start event for the 10-business-day clock. Parallel deemed-receipt rule at 950 CMR 32.06(2)(e). clock_effect kept 'none' as this is a calculation defining the start, not itself a deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Clock runs only for compliant requests
rules.atomic_rule: Calculation of time commences only for requests made in accordance with the request requirements (e.g., reasonable description, proper delivery).
rules.trigger: A request is received that does or does not meet the request requirements.
rules.source_language: calculation of time will commence only for requests that are made in accordance with 950 CMR 32.06(1).

rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must permit inspection or furnish a copy (or any segregable portion) not later than 10 business days following receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a valid request.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of request
rules.source_language: shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record ... or any segregable portion of a public record, not later than 10 business days following the receipt of the request
rules.notes: Core response window. Fixed by statute (10 business days); the city does not vary it.

rules.atomic_rule: Independent of the 10-day cap, production or inspection must occur at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a valid request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay" from request receipt
rules.source_language: shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record
rules.notes: Soft/undefined standard; do not convert to a day count. Config Home structural (a standard the engine applies).

rules.atomic_rule: If the entity will not fully produce within the initial timeframe (or will withhold), it must inform the requestor in writing not later than 10 business days after initial receipt.
rules.trigger: Entity does not intend to permit inspection/copy within subsection (a), or the request unduly burdens it.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from initial receipt of request
rules.source_language: the agency or municipality shall inform the requestor in writing not later than 10 business days after the initial receipt of the request for public records. The written response shall be made via first class or electronic mail

rules.legal_concept: Required contents of the written response
rules.atomic_rule: The § 10(b) written response must contain nine enumerated elements: receipt confirmation; records not in custody; other custodian; records withheld with specific exemptions; records to be produced with a burden statement; a reasonable production timeframe; a suggested scope modification; an itemized good-faith fee estimate; and a statement of appeal and judicial-review rights.
rules.trigger: A § 10(b) written response is triggered.
rules.source_language: The written response shall ... (i) confirm receipt of the request; ... (iv) identify any records, categories of records or portions of records that the agency or municipality intends to withhold, and provide the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption or exemptions upon which the withholding is based ... (vi) identify a reasonable timeframe in which the agency or municipality shall produce the public records sought ... (vii) suggest a reasonable modification of the scope of the request ... (viii) include an itemized, good faith estimate of any fees that may be charged to produce the records; and (ix) include a statement informing the requestor of the right of appeal to the supervisor of records under subsection (a) of section 10A and the right to seek judicial review
rules.notes: Kept as one structural notice with its mandatory content set; distinct parametric/clock components (extended timeframe, fee estimate) are split into their own rows.

rules.atomic_rule: For a municipality, the reasonable production timeframe stated in the written response shall not exceed 25 business days following initial receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Municipality invokes the § 10(b) extended-timeframe path.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 25 business-days from initial receipt (municipality)
rules.source_language: provided, that for an agency, the timeframe shall not exceed 15 business days following the initial receipt of the request for public records and for a municipality the timeframe shall not exceed 25 business days following the initial receipt of the request for public records
rules.notes: Municipal ceiling. Same concept as MA-0021 (agency, 15 bd) with different actor/value.

rules.atomic_rule: For a (state) agency, the reasonable production timeframe stated in the written response shall not exceed 15 business days following initial receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Agency invokes the § 10(b) extended-timeframe path.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 15 business-days from initial receipt (agency)
rules.source_language: provided, that for an agency, the timeframe shall not exceed 15 business days following the initial receipt of the request for public records
rules.notes: Agency variant of the same ceiling concept. Included for completeness; municipal build uses MA-0020.
