rules.atomic_rule: The requestor may voluntarily agree to a response date beyond the statutory extended timeframes.
rules.trigger: Requestor agrees to a later response date.
rules.source_language: provided further, that the requestor may voluntarily agree to a response date beyond the timeframes set forth herein
rules.notes: A branch that extends the applicable deadline by mutual agreement; not a numeric value.

rules.legal_concept: RAO petition to Supervisor for extension
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may petition the Supervisor of Records for an extension of time as soon as practical and within 20 business days after initial receipt (or within 10 business days after a Supervisor determination that the record is public).
rules.trigger: Magnitude/difficulty of the request or multiple requests unduly burdens the entity so it cannot complete within the § 10(b)(vi) time.
rules.clock_spec: within 20 business-days from initial receipt (or 10 business-days from Supervisor determination)
rules.source_language: a records access officer may, as soon as practical and within 20 business days after initial receipt of the request, or within 10 business days after receipt of a determination by the supervisor of public records that the requested record constitutes a public record, petition the supervisor of records for an extension of the time
rules.notes: Structural extension path with a filing deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Copy of extension petition to requestor
rules.atomic_rule: Upon submitting the extension petition to the Supervisor, the RAO must furnish a copy of the petition to the requestor.
rules.trigger: RAO submits an extension petition.
rules.source_language: The records access officer shall, upon submitting the petition to the supervisor of records, furnish a copy of the petition to the requestor.

rules.atomic_rule: Upon a showing of good cause, the Supervisor may grant a single extension to a municipality not to exceed 30 business days.
rules.trigger: Supervisor finds good cause on an RAO extension petition.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: single extension up to 30 business-days (municipality)
rules.source_language: Upon a showing of good cause, the supervisor of records may grant a single extension to an agency not to exceed 20 business days and a single extension to a municipality not to exceed 30 business days.
rules.notes: Municipal variant; single extension only.

rules.atomic_rule: Upon a showing of good cause, the Supervisor may grant a single extension to a (state) agency not to exceed 20 business days.
rules.trigger: Supervisor finds good cause on an RAO extension petition.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: single extension up to 20 business-days (agency)
rules.source_language: the supervisor of records may grant a single extension to an agency not to exceed 20 business days
rules.notes: Agency variant of the same ceiling concept.

rules.atomic_rule: The Supervisor must issue a written decision on an RAO extension petition within 5 business days following receipt of the petition.
rules.trigger: Supervisor receives an RAO extension petition.
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from Supervisor's receipt of the petition
rules.source_language: The supervisor of records shall issue a written decision regarding a petition submitted by a records access officer under this subsection within 5 business days following receipt of the petition.

rules.atomic_rule: If the Supervisor finds a request is part of a series of contemporaneous requests that are frivolous or designed to intimidate/harass and not for broad public dissemination, the Supervisor may grant a longer extension or relieve the entity of its obligation to provide copies.
rules.trigger: Supervisor's finding of a frivolous/harassing contemporaneous request series.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: obligation to provide copies may be relieved (or a longer extension granted)
rules.source_language: If the supervisor of records determines that the request is part of a series of contemporaneous requests that are frivolous or designed to intimidate or harass, and the requests are not intended for the broad dissemination of information to the public about actual or alleged government activity, the supervisor of records may grant a longer extension or relieve the agency or municipality of its obligation to provide copies of the records sought.
rules.notes: A terminal branch (request obligation may end) available only via Supervisor determination.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee not to exceed actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may assess a reasonable fee for production (except freely-inspectable records), and the fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record.
rules.trigger: RAO produces records that are not freely available for inspection.
rules.source_language: A records access officer may assess a reasonable fee for the production of a public record except those records that are freely available for public inspection. The reasonable fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record.
rules.notes: Overall ceiling under which the itemized fee components sit.

rules.atomic_rule: The fee for standard black-and-white paper copies or printouts shall not exceed 5 cents per page, for both single- and double-sided copies.
rules.trigger: RAO provides paper copies/printouts.
rules.source_language: the fee assessed for standard black and white paper copies or printouts of records shall not exceed 5 cents per page, for both single and double-sided black and white copies or printouts
rules.notes: Ceiling $0.05/page. City may charge at or below.

rules.atomic_rule: The actual cost of any storage device or material provided in response to a request may be included as part of the fee.
rules.trigger: RAO provides records on a storage device/material.
rules.source_language: the actual cost of any storage device or material provided to a person in response to a request for public records under subsection (a) may be included as part of the fee

rules.atomic_rule: For a municipality, the hourly labor rate must equal or be less than the lowest-paid capable employee's rate and shall not exceed $25 per hour, unless a higher rate is approved by the Supervisor.
rules.trigger: Municipality devotes more than 2 hours of employee time to a request.
rules.source_language: if a municipality is required to devote more than 2 hours of employee time to search for, compile, segregate, redact or reproduce a record requested, the records access officer may include as part of the fee an hourly rate equal to or less than the hourly rate attributed to the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill required to search for, compile, segregate, redact or reproduce the record requested but the fee (A) shall not be more than $25 per hour unless such rate is approved by the supervisor of records under clause (iv)
rules.notes: Municipal ceiling $25/hr; may be exceeded only with Supervisor approval (MA-0037).

rules.atomic_rule: For a (state) agency, the hourly labor rate must equal or be less than the lowest-paid capable employee's rate and shall not be more than $25 per hour.
rules.trigger: Agency devotes more than 4 hours of employee time to a request.
rules.source_language: if an agency is required to devote more than 4 hours of employee time ... the records access officer may also include as part of the fee an hourly rate equal to or less than the hourly rate attributed to the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill ... but the fee (A) shall not be more than $25 per hour
rules.notes: Agency variant of the same ceiling concept (agency cannot exceed $25/hr even with approval).

rules.atomic_rule: For a municipality with a population over 20,000, no labor fee may be assessed for the first 2 hours of work performed.
rules.trigger: Municipality (population over 20,000) performs request labor.
rules.source_language: (B) shall not be assessed for the first 2 hours of work performed where the responding municipality has a population of over 20,000 people
rules.notes: Free-hour threshold (2 hrs) applies only to municipalities over 20,000 population; municipalities of 20,000 or fewer are not entitled to charge labor at all under the structure and the 2-hour free tier is population-gated.

rules.atomic_rule: For a (state) agency, no labor fee may be assessed for the first 4 hours of work performed.
rules.trigger: Agency performs request labor.
rules.source_language: (B) shall not be assessed for the first 4 hours of work performed
rules.notes: Agency variant of the same free-hours concept (4 hrs).

rules.atomic_rule: A fee shall not be assessed for time spent segregating or redacting records unless such segregation/redaction is required by law or approved by the Supervisor.
rules.trigger: Entity spends time segregating or redacting records.
rules.source_language: (C) shall not be assessed for time spent segregating or redacting records unless such segregation or redaction is required by law or approved by the supervisor of records under clause (iv)
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.07(2)(d).

rules.legal_concept: Supervisor approval for redaction charge / excess rate
rules.atomic_rule: The Supervisor may approve a petition to charge for segregation/redaction time, or a municipal petition to charge over $25/hour, if the request is for a commercial purpose or the fee is a necessary, reasonable good-faith cost not designed to deter access; the entity must furnish the petition to the requestor and the Supervisor decides within 5 business days.
rules.trigger: Agency/municipality petitions the Supervisor to charge redaction time or exceed $25/hr.
rules.clock_spec: Supervisor written determination within 5 business-days of receipt of the petition
rules.source_language: the supervisor of records may approve a petition from an agency or municipality to charge for time spent segregating or redacting, or a petition from a municipality to charge in excess of $25 per hour, if the supervisor of records determines that (A) the request is for a commercial purpose; or (B) the fee represents an actual and good faith representation by the agency or municipality to comply with the request, the fee is necessary such that the request could not have been prudently completed without the redaction, segregation or fee in excess of $25 per hour and the amount of the fee is reasonable and the fee is not designed to limit, deter or prevent access
rules.notes: Structural fee-petition path; the 5-business-day decision clock is stated in § 10(d)(iv)(3). Contains a multi-factor test kept intact per grain rule.

rules.atomic_rule: The RAO may waive or reduce a fee upon a showing that disclosure is in the public interest (likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government and not primarily in the requestor's commercial interest), or that the requestor lacks the financial ability to pay the full reasonable fee.
rules.trigger: Requestor shows public interest or inability to pay.
rules.source_language: the records access officer may waive or reduce the amount of any fee charged under this subsection upon a showing that disclosure of a requested record is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requestor, or upon a showing that the requestor lacks the financial ability to pay the full amount of the reasonable fee

rules.atomic_rule: If fees are to be assessed, the RAO must provide a written, itemized, good-faith estimate of fees before complying, within the 10-business-day response.
rules.trigger: Fees will be charged for a request.
rules.source_language: if fees are being assessed, a records access officer shall provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate of any fees that may be charged to produce the records prior to complying with a public records request within ten business days.
rules.notes: Statutory basis at M.G.L. c. 66, § 10(b)(viii).

rules.legal_concept: No fee unless timely written response
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the RAO responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).
rules.trigger: RAO failed to provide the § 10(b) response within 10 business days.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: fee right is forfeited if no § 10(b) response within 10 business-days
rules.source_language: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).
rules.notes: Strong operational consequence tied to the response clock; regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.06(2)(c). clock_effect terminal reflects the loss of the fee entitlement.

rules.atomic_rule: The RAO may deny public-records requests from a requester who has failed to compensate the entity for previously produced public records.
rules.trigger: Requester has an unpaid balance for previously produced records.
rules.source_language: the records access officer may deny public records requests from a requester who has failed to compensate the agency or municipality for previously produced public records

rules.atomic_rule: When denying for an unpaid balance, the RAO shall provide written notification detailing the reasons, including an itemized list of balances attributed to previously produced records.
rules.trigger: RAO denies a request under the unpaid-balance provision.
rules.source_language: the records access officer shall provide a written notification to the requester detailing the reasons behind the denial, including an itemized list of any balances attributed to previously produced records

rules.legal_concept: Payment of reasonable fee as precondition
rules.atomic_rule: The production duty is conditioned on the RAO receiving payment of a reasonable fee as set forth in subsection (d).
rules.trigger: A fee is properly assessed for a request.
rules.source_language: (iii) the records access officer receives payment of a reasonable fee as set forth in subsection (d).

rules.legal_concept: Delay of production pending full payment
rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may delay provision of records until all fees related to the request are paid in full by the person seeking access.
rules.trigger: Assessed fees remain unpaid.
rules.source_language: a records access officer may delay provision of records until all fees related to such requests are paid in full by the person seeking access to the requested records in accordance with 950 CMR 32.07.

rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must furnish any segregable portion of a public record (i.e., disclose non-exempt portions even where other portions are withheld).
rules.trigger: A record contains both disclosable and withheld/exempt portions.
rules.source_language: shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record ... or any segregable portion of a public record

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a new record
rules.atomic_rule: The RAO is not required to create a new public record to comply with a request; furnishing a segregable portion of an existing record is not creation of a new record.
rules.trigger: A request would require creating a record that does not exist.
rules.source_language: The records access officer shall not be required to create a new public record in order to comply with a request, provided that furnishing a segregable portion of a public record shall not be deemed to be creation of a new record.
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.07(1)(f).

rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must provide public records by electronic means unless the record is not available in electronic form or the requestor cannot receive/access a usable electronic form.
rules.trigger: Records are available in electronic form and the requestor can receive them electronically.
rules.source_language: The records access officer shall provide the public records to a requestor by electronic means unless the record is not available in electronic form or the requestor does not have the ability to receive or access the records in a usable electronic form.

rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must, to the extent feasible, provide the record in the requestor's preferred format or, absent a preference, in a searchable, machine-readable format.
rules.trigger: Requestor states (or does not state) a format preference.
rules.source_language: The records access officer shall, to the extent feasible, provide the public record in the requestor's preferred format or, in the absence of a preferred format, in a searchable, machine readable format.

rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must provide electronic records in native form when possible, presuming machine-readable electronic copies unless the requester specifies otherwise.
rules.trigger: Electronic records are requested.
rules.source_language: the records access officer shall presume that a requester prefers copies provided in machine-readable electronic form, when electronic form is available, unless the requester specifies an alternative preference. the records access officer must provide electronic records in native form when possible.

rules.atomic_rule: A person shall not be required to make a personal inspection of a record prior to receiving a copy.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks copies without inspecting first.
rules.source_language: a person shall not be required to make a personal inspection of the record prior to receiving a copy.

rules.atomic_rule: As an alternative to receiving copies, the requester shall be permitted, to the extent feasible and at reasonable times, to view/inspect records before obtaining copies or to use a personal device such as a camera or portable scanner to copy records.
rules.trigger: Requester elects to inspect or self-copy.
rules.source_language: as an alternative to obtaining copies of records from a records access officer a requester shall be permitted, to the extent feasible, and at reasonable times: 1. view and inspect records prior to obtaining copies; or 2. use a personal device such as a camera or portable scanner to copy records.

rules.atomic_rule: The RAO must provide written notice by first class or electronic mail of any denial of access, within 10 business days of receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: RAO denies access to any requested record.
rules.clock_spec: within 10 business-days of receipt of the request
rules.source_language: a records access officer shall provide written notice by first class mail or electronic mail to a requester of any denial of access to records. a records access officer shall provide such written notice of denial of access within ten business days of its receipt of a request for public records
rules.notes: Denial-notice deadline coincides with the § 10(b) 10-business-day response clock.

rules.atomic_rule: A denial/withholding must identify the records withheld and provide the specific reasons, including the specific statutory exemption(s) or common-law privilege and its applicability to each withheld portion.
rules.trigger: Records or portions are withheld.
rules.source_language: identify any records, categories of records or portions of records that the agency or municipality intends to withhold, and provide the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption or exemptions upon which the withholding is based
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.06(3)(c)5-6 requires identifying each cited exemption/privilege and its applicability to each withheld portion.

rules.atomic_rule: Where a record is withheld on a claim of attorney-client privilege, the written denial must provide a detailed description of the record, including the names of the author and recipients and, in general terms, the subject matter of the withheld information.
rules.trigger: Withholding based on attorney-client privilege.
rules.source_language: where a record has been withheld based on a claim of the attorney-client privilege the records access officer shall provide in its written denial a detailed description of the record, including the names of the author and recipients, and in general terms, the subject matter of the withheld information.
rules.notes: Aligns with M.G.L. c. 66, § 10A(a) requiring a detailed description in lieu of in camera inspection for privileged records on appeal. Flag for human legal review.

rules.legal_concept: Notice of appeal and judicial-review rights
rules.atomic_rule: The response/denial must include a statement informing the requester of the right of administrative appeal to the Supervisor under § 10A(a) and the right to seek judicial review by civil action in the superior court.
rules.trigger: A written response or denial is issued.
rules.source_language: include a statement informing the requestor of the right of appeal to the supervisor of records under subsection (a) of section 10A and the right to seek judicial review of an unfavorable decision by commencing a civil action in the superior court under subsection (c) of section 10A.
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.06(3)(c)8.

rules.atomic_rule: In all proceedings, there is a presumption that the record sought is public; on judicial review the burden is on the agency/municipality to prove by a preponderance that the record may be withheld.
rules.trigger: A dispute or proceeding over disclosability.
rules.source_language: In all proceedings pursuant to 950 CMR 32.00, there shall be a presumption that the record sought is public.
rules.notes: Statutory burden allocation at M.G.L. c. 66, § 10A(d)(1)(iv).

rules.legal_concept: Administrative appeal to Supervisor of Records
rules.atomic_rule: If an entity fails to comply with § 10 or issues a response the requestor believes violates § 10, the person who submitted the initial request may petition the Supervisor of Records for a determination whether a violation has occurred.
rules.trigger: Non-compliance with § 10 or a response believed to violate § 10.
rules.source_language: If an agency or municipality fails to comply with a requirement of section 10 or issues a response the requestor believes in violation of section 10, the person who submitted the initial request for public records may petition the supervisor of records for a determination as to whether a violation has occurred.
rules.notes: Administrative-appeal path (namespaced appeal.administrative).

rules.atomic_rule: A petition appealing a records access officer's response must be filed with the Supervisor within 90 calendar days of the date of the response.
rules.trigger: RAO issues a response the requester wishes to appeal.
rules.clock_spec: 90 calendar-days from the date of the RAO response
rules.source_language: petitions for appeal of a response by a records access officer must be made within 90 calendar days of the date of the response by a records access officer.

rules.atomic_rule: A petition appealing a failure to respond within the required timeframes must be filed with the Supervisor within 90 calendar days of the request.
rules.trigger: RAO fails to respond within the timeliness requirements.
rules.clock_spec: 90 calendar-days from the date of the request
rules.source_language: petitions for appeal of a failure to respond within the timeliness requirements of 950 CMR 32.00 must be made within 90 calendar days of the request.

rules.atomic_rule: All appeal petitions must be in writing and specifically describe the nature of the requester's objections to the response or failure to timely respond.
rules.trigger: Requester files an administrative appeal.
rules.source_language: all petitions for appeal shall be in writing and shall specifically describe the nature of the requester's objections to the response or failure to timely respond.

rules.legal_concept: Copy of appeal petition to RAO
rules.atomic_rule: In petitioning the Supervisor, the requester must provide a copy of the petition to the records access officer associated with the petition.
rules.trigger: Requester files an administrative appeal.
rules.source_language: in petitioning the Supervisor, the requester shall provide a copy of such petition to the records access officer associated with such petition.

rules.atomic_rule: The Supervisor of Records must issue a written determination on any properly submitted appeal petition not later than 10 business days following receipt of the petition.
rules.trigger: Supervisor receives an appeal petition.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from Supervisor's receipt of the petition
rules.source_language: The supervisor of records shall issue a written determination regarding any petition submitted in accordance with this section not later than 10 business days following receipt of the petition by the supervisor of records.
rules.notes: Regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.08(2)(a).

rules.legal_concept: Supervisor order of relief on violation
rules.atomic_rule: Upon determining that a violation has occurred, the Supervisor shall order timely and appropriate relief.
rules.trigger: Supervisor determines a violation occurred.
rules.source_language: Upon a determination by the supervisor of records that a violation has occurred, the supervisor of records shall order timely and appropriate relief.

rules.atomic_rule: An oral request, while valid as a public-records request, cannot be the basis of an administrative appeal to the Supervisor.
rules.trigger: Requester who made an oral request attempts to appeal.
rules.source_language: an oral request, while valid as a public record request, shall not be the basis of an appeal under 950 CMR 32.08.

rules.legal_concept: Grounds for Supervisor to deny an appeal
rules.atomic_rule: The Supervisor may deny an appeal for reasons including that the records are the subject of active litigation/administrative hearing/mediation, the request is designed to harass/intimidate or assist a crime, the request is made solely for a commercial purpose, or the requester failed to comply with request requirements.
rules.trigger: Supervisor evaluates an appeal petition.
rules.source_language: the Supervisor may deny an appeal for, among other reasons if, in the opinion of the Supervisor: 1. the public records in question are the subjects of disputes in active litigation, administrative hearings or mediation; 2. the request is designed or intended to harass, intimidate, or assist in the commission of a crime; 3. the public records request is made solely for a commercial purpose;
rules.notes: Non-exhaustive discretionary grounds; supervisor-side branch.

rules.atomic_rule: A requestor aggrieved by a Supervisor order, or by the Supervisor's failure to issue a timely determination, may obtain judicial review only through a superior court action in the nature of certiorari under c. 249, § 4.
rules.trigger: Aggrieved by Supervisor order or by an untimely Supervisor determination.
rules.source_language: A requestor, aggrieved by an order issued by the supervisor of records or upon the failure of the supervisor of records to issue a timely determination, may obtain judicial review only through an action in superior court seeking relief in the nature of certiorari under section 4 of chapter 249 and as prescribed in subsection (d).
rules.notes: Judicial-review path (namespaced appeal.judicial). c. 249 § 4 certiorari carries its own filing deadline (generally 60 days), not restated here.

rules.atomic_rule: Notwithstanding the Supervisor and AG procedures, a requestor may initiate a civil action to enforce the chapter, filed for municipalities in the superior court of the county where the municipality is located.
rules.trigger: Requestor elects direct court enforcement.
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding the procedure in subsections (a) or (b), a requestor may initiate a civil action to enforce the requirements of this chapter. Any action under this subsection shall be filed in Suffolk superior court with respect to agencies and, with respect to municipalities, in the superior court in the county in which the municipality is located.
rules.notes: Independent judicial path; does not require exhausting the Supervisor appeal.

rules.legal_concept: De novo review; public-record presumption; burden
rules.atomic_rule: In a requestor's civil action, the superior court determines the propriety of the withholding de novo, a presumption exists that each record is public, and the burden is on the defendant entity to prove by a preponderance that the record may be withheld under state or federal law.
rules.trigger: A civil enforcement action is filed.
rules.source_language: a presumption shall exist that each record sought is public and the burden shall be on the defendant agency or municipality to prove, by a preponderance of the evidence, that such record or portion of the record may be withheld in accordance with state or federal law.

rules.atomic_rule: If an entity refuses or fails to comply with a Supervisor order, the Supervisor may notify the Attorney General, who may take measures necessary to ensure compliance.
rules.trigger: Entity refuses/fails to comply with a Supervisor order.
rules.source_language: If an agency or municipality refuses or fails to comply with an order issued by the supervisor of records, the supervisor of records may notify the attorney general who, after consultation with the supervisor of records, may take whatever measures the attorney general considers necessary to ensure compliance.
rules.notes: Enforcement trigger only; the AG's remedial measures and any damages amounts are excluded per the inclusion test.

structural_branches.description: The M.G.L. c. 66 s.10(b) written response is a mandatory branch triggered when the entity cannot fully produce within the initial timeframe or intends to withhold; it carries nine required content elements (MA-0019).

RAO petition to the Supervisor of Records for a single time extension - a bespoke MA stage inserted between the initial response and production, gated by a 20-business-day filing window and a 5-business-day Supervisor decision (MA-0023, MA-0025/26, MA-0027).
Supervisor may relieve the entity of its obligation to provide copies where a contemporaneous request series is frivolous/harassing - a terminal path ending the request (MA-0028).
Entity petition to the Supervisor to charge for redaction time or (municipality) to exceed $25/hr - a MA-specific fee-approval branch with its own 5-business-day decision clock (MA-0037).

Administrative appeal to the Supervisor of Records (Division of Public Records) - MA's internal review stage before court, with 90-day filing windows and a 10-business-day determination (MA-0057 through MA-0065).
Certiorari review in superior court under c. 249 s.4 of a Supervisor order or untimely determination - MA's designated judicial-review route (MA-0066).
Direct de novo civil enforcement action in superior court, available without exhausting the Supervisor appeal (MA-0067, MA-0068).
Supervisor referral to the Attorney General on non-compliance with a Supervisor order (MA-0069).
Designated records access officer (municipal clerk by default) as the routing/response locus for all municipal requests (MA-0010, MA-0011, MA-0012).

material_negatives.note: MA has no automatic 'silence = denial' or 'silence = grant' deeming provision for a municipality's non-response. Instead, failure to respond within the required timeframe opens the administrative-appeal path (petition to the Supervisor within 90 calendar days of the request, 950 CMR 32.08(1)(e)) and enables judicial review upon the Supervisor's failure to issue a timely determination (M.G.L. c. 66, s.10A(a)). Absence of a found deeming rule is not proof none exists.

No explicit statutory preservation/litigation-hold triggered by the request or by an appeal on that request was found in c. 66 s.10/s.10A or 950 CMR 32.00. Records retention is governed separately (records-retention schedules, out of scope under the inclusion test).

MA provides no separate 'acknowledgment' step distinct from substantive action; the s.10(b) written response (which confirms receipt) and the s.10(a) production duty both run on the same 10-business-day clock. Acknowledgment is folded into MA-0016/MA-0018 rather than being an independent deadline.

No fixed statewide per-unit fee for electronic records; electronic production is governed by the general 'actual cost of reproducing' ceiling (MA-0029) plus the labor-rate structure. No separate electronic-record rate parameter exists to configure.

No statute or regulation found requiring municipalities to assign or maintain a tracking/reference number for individual requests. (The Supervisor's own appeal intake is time-stamped under 950 CMR 32.08(1)(j), but that governs the Division, not the municipal RAO.)

MA sets no numeric deposit threshold triggering mandatory prepayment; the RAO 'may delay provision of records until all fees ... are paid in full' (MA-0044) but no dollar threshold or advance-deposit percentage is specified to configure.
